imagePrompt: A teenage girl on a putting green that is not the correct green for her hole, preparing to drop a golf ball just off the green with a wedge.
imageAlt: Teen girl golfer about to drop a ball from the edge of a putting green, preparing for free relief.

issues: The golf ball is depicted in midair as it is being dropped, which is correct and natural.
The club in hand appears to be a wedge and is realistic in size and form.
The golfer is a teenage boy, with a medium white skin tone, blue top, and purple shorts, matching requirements.
Golf posture is plausible for dropping from knee height.
Only one golf ball is visible; no extra clubs or items are in the scene.

The golfer holds the club in the left hand, but the dropping motion is done with the left hand as well; for a left-handed golfer, the dropping should be with the right hand per the prompt for better clarity.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Adjust the golfer's posture so they are dropping the golf ball from knee height using their right hand, while holding the wedge naturally in their left hand to clearly indicate left-handedness.

questions.title: Your ball stops on the wrong green
questions.question: You hit your ball, and it stops on a putting green for a different hole. What should you do?

choices.text: Hit the ball from where it is to be quick
Pick up your ball and throw it off the green
Pick up your ball and drop it off the green, not nearer to the flag
Ask to get a penalty and try your shot again

questions.explanation: If your ball stops on the wrong green, you must pick it up and drop it off the green, closer to where you came from but not nearer to the flag you are playing to.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short, smooth grass area around the hole where you try to putt the ball in.
Letting the ball go from knee height so it falls to the ground.

questions.teachingTip: Remind children that they must never play a shot from a green that isn’t the one for their hole. Show them where to drop their ball if this happens.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think it is okay to play from the wrong green to save time.
Some might think they should throw the ball instead of dropping it properly.
They might not know what 'no closer to the hole' means.

questions.title: Ball lands on the wrong green
questions.question: If your ball comes to rest on a putting green that’s not the one for the hole you’re playing, what should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies to save time
Pick up the ball and throw it off the green
Take free relief by dropping the ball off the green, no closer to the hole
Ask for a penalty and replay the shot

questions.explanation: You must take free relief by dropping your ball off the wrong green, no closer to the hole, and may not play from another putting green.
